content.text: component of fungal cell membranes and alters permeability to allow leakage of ions and other intracellular components → cell death
May be either fungistatic or fungicidal, depending on tissue concentration achieved and organism susceptibility
: broadest spectrum of coverage of all the antifungals
: infusion reactions (fever/chills, HA, malaise, rigors, BP changes, thrombophlebitis, N/V), nephrotoxicity, decreased K & Mg, anemia, back/chest pain (AmBisome)
Use severely limited due to extensive toxicities
: medication errors related to confusion in dosing of conventional vs liposomal formulations have resulted in death – ODs can result in cardiopulmonary arrest

: interfering with purine and pyrimidine uptake and by deaminated to 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) and then converted to 5-fluorodeoxyuridylic acid monophosphate, a noncompetitive inhibitor of thymidylate synthetase which interferes with DNA synthesis

: USED IN COMBO W/ AMPHOTERICIN B – treatment of systemic mycoses and meningitis caused by Cryptococcus neoformans and Candida; 5FC + amphoB = gold standard for tx of HIV-associated cryptococcal meningitis
: dose-related myelosuppression (neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, anemia), reversible hepatic dysfunction, GI disturbances, worsening renal failure
: use extreme caution in pts w/ renal dysfunction
); limited against C. glabrata; C. krusei is resistant; not as effective vs. aspergillosis as other agents in this class
: GI, HA, rash, increased hepatic enzymes, NO endocrine side effects
: not recommended during pregnancy, can cause exfoliative skin disorders
: GI, rash, HA, HTN, hepatic dysfunction
: can cause or worsen HF, QT prolongation

roles.drugs: Induction: IV liposomal amphotericin B + oral flucytosine, 2 weeks with advanced HIV (2–4 weeks without HIV); amphotericin B deoxycholate if no lipid form
Advanced HIV: single high-dose IV liposomal amphotericin B on day 1 + oral flucytosine and fluconazole for 2 weeks
Maintenance: oral fluconazole (6–12 months without HIV; with HIV until CD4 >100 on ART). Itraconazole at the same dose is acceptable (check levels)
